analysis.title: "Only Fear Is Of The Right-Tail": McElligott Shows Why The S&P Is Blind To The Carnage Beneath It
key_insights: The S&P has moved less than 1% since early August, after the July momentum de-gross and AI unwind. Index-level vol is very low and single stocks are moving sharply, so the index looks calm while most members are falling.

The best trade this year is 'Long the AI Core Constraints': long semis plus long energy and commodities. The pair is up 65% YTD on a 3.2 Sharpe. The classic 60/40 portfolio is up about 8% with a 1.2 Sharpe, and bonds have not worked as a long or as a hedge to equities.

SPX realized vol is 7 (10-day), 10 (1-month) and 9.5 (2-month). 3-month ATM implied vol is at the 2nd percentile (1Y), 25-delta put/call skew is at the 0.4th percentile (1Y), and the 1DTE ATM straddle is at the 9th percentile (2Y).

Implied correlation is at the 1.8th percentile and realized correlation at the 0.7th percentile. McElligott calls this 'High Dispersion = Low Correlation'. Goldman's Brian Garrett noted only two other periods in 25 years had realized correlation this low.

Market breadth is extremely narrow. Ten stocks drove 70% of the S&P's 23% rally since March 30, with Nvidia responsible for 13% and Micron, Apple and Microsoft about 9% each. The other 490 stocks account for 30%.

Over the past month the SPX moved 0.8% while the average stock moved 8.9%. That 8.1% spread is in the 95th percentile of the past 30 years. AMD (+39.5%) and Intel (+27.6%) are winners, Netflix (-18.2%) and the banks are laggards.

McElligott argues equities are already in a 'rolling correction' driven by rates-sensitive sectors and by crowding-out of capital and sentiment for 'AI losers'. Over 30 days only TMT and Energy are positive. Declines: Healthcare -3.5%, Consumer Discretionary -3.6%, Utilities -4.6%, Industrials -5.8%, Financials -7.7%, Materials -7.9%, REITs -9.8%.
85% of S&P 500 names are more than 10% below their all-time highs, 59% more than 20% below, 41% more than 30% below, 26% more than 40% below and 17% more than 50% below.

Vol sellers are keeping the index pinned. Nomura's 0DTE customer gamma is +$14 billion (100th percentile), attributed to QIS volatility-risk-premium strategies. Daily 25-delta put selling has a 10-day Sharpe of 13.9 and a daily strangle 14.2.
Derivatives/income fund AUM is $322 billion, up $222 billion since 2020. Combined fund and exotic vega supply is about 415 million vega per month, adding to dealer vega supply.
Low realized vol has let vol-scaling systematic funds re-lever. Vol Control, CTA and Risk Parity combined US equity exposure is back to the 86th percentile, near the year's highs.

Nobody is buying downside protection. SPX call skew is at the 99.6th percentile, because investors with low net exposure fear missing a narrow AI-led rally more than a drop. Many are under-captured in the AI sleeve.

The bull case rests on 'AI Capex Trickle-Down' into earnings of the 'Other 493', plus nominal GDP of 7% to 9% (nowcast 7.05%). The Mag 7 contribution to S&P earnings growth fell from 15% to 7% in Q2 while the Other 493 accelerated from 7% to 13% and then 18%.

Energy is the fragile link. Europe and Asia are short energy and the world ex Asia/India is short refinery capacity. A European emergency diesel release buys only a little over a month of supply. McElligott's rule is 'Cracks = Rate Vol'.
EU diesel cracks at 85 and EUR 1y1y rate vol at 112.6 have moved almost tick for tick since February. European energy prices are near the year's highs.

McElligott's three trade permutations: chase the right tail with MegaCap Tech call spreads into earnings, fade the energy premium on any Iran peace talk, and own long USD/EUR rates vega via long-dated swaption straddles.

Within hours of the note, Trump said the US will not attack Iran before the midterms, and oil fell. McElligott had flagged this conciliatory outcome as one binary. The FT then reported OpenAI's annualized revenue is roughly $20 billion below what was signalled to investors, and the Nasdaq fell more than 1%.

The article's author disagrees with McElligott's base case and thinks a Garrett-style 'starburst' (a correlation-driven selloff) is likelier than an 'SPX 8k' rally. The author sees McElligott's swaption straddles as the cheapest insurance.

sector_views.sector: Technology, Media and Telecom (semis, AI constraints)
sector_views.rationale: TMT is one of only two S&P sectors positive over 30 days. The world is 'Short Compute', so long semis is part of the best trade YTD.
Energy is the other positive sector and a hedge for AI longs. Refinery shortages keep cracks high, but a peace headline could sharply cut the energy premium.

sector_views.sector: REITs, Materials, Financials, Industrials, Utilities, Consumer Discretionary, Healthcare
sector_views.rationale: All fell over 30 days (REITs -9.8% to Healthcare -3.5%), hurt by rates sensitivity and crowding-out of capital toward AI winners.

earnings_insights: Mag 7 contribution to S&P earnings growth fell from 15% to 7% in Q2, while the Other 493 accelerated from 7% in Q4 2025 to 13% and then 18% (growth contribution as cited by Nomura, basis not specified).

McElligott's bull case is that AI capex trickles down into 'Other 493' earnings, with the market expecting upside from earnings season kicking off next week. He sees buyside investors underpositioned for a strong AI earnings rally.

macro_indicators.interpretation: McElligott argues strong nominal growth lets corporates and equities 'absorb the Rates'.
Moves nearly tick for tick with EUR 1y1y rate vol since February, so rates traders are effectively trading diesel.
Elevated rate vol is linked to energy shortage fears and keeps bonds from working as an equity hedge.

macro_indicators.reading: Likely to go higher, repricing Fed path into 'restrictive' territory
macro_indicators.interpretation: McElligott's basis for owning rates vega even in a strong-earnings scenario.

trade_ideas.description: Buy MegaCap Tech call spreads into the earnings rally over the next month
trade_ideas.rationale: 99th percentile call skew 'doesn't hurt' and the buyside is underpositioned for an 'SPX 8k' move if AI earnings lift all boats.
trade_ideas.risk: The AI demand premise is under pressure after the FT report on OpenAI revenue, and the rally is concentrated in ten stocks.

trade_ideas.description: Fade the energy premium on Iran peace talk, with trades in Gold and IWM upside
trade_ideas.rationale: Any conciliatory Trump Iran deal talk into the midterms would see energy and rate vol 'SMOKED off recent levels'.
trade_ideas.risk: 'Before the midterms' is not 'never', and refining capacity constraints persist regardless of oil flows.

trade_ideas.description: Own long-dated USD/EUR rates vega through long-dated swaption straddles
trade_ideas.rationale: Terminal rate expectations likely go higher even in a great-earnings world, and the Fed path must reprice toward restrictive territory.
trade_ideas.risk: A growth scare from higher rates and energy breaking something, though tail funds are hedging that with low-strike receivers and curve caps.

trade_ideas.description: Long the AI Core Constraints: long semis plus long energy and commodities
trade_ideas.rationale: The world is short compute and short energy/infrastructure, and the pair has a built-in rates hedge.
trade_ideas.risk: Peace headlines hitting energy, or a weaker AI demand story hitting semis.

risk_factors: A further energy price shock from resumed attacks or a US diesel ban in a few months could trigger a rates tantrum.
Higher rates and energy prices could 'Break Something', causing demand destruction and a growth scare.
Extremely low realized correlation has only two precedents in 25 years, which the article ties to the run-up to the GFC and Volmageddon.
The index rally depends on ten stocks and the premise that AI demand is real and growing, which the FT report on OpenAI revenue challenges.
Dealer gamma and income-fund vol supply could reverse and amplify a move, and short-vol strategies carry steamroller risk.
AI capex financing parade (OpenAI seeking $50 billion for AVGO chips, ORCL/Apollo/GS chip financing) and the Anthropic IPO uncertainty.

US midterm elections on November 3 are a key date for energy and rates risk.

tension_points.bull_case: Underpositioned beta is forced to chase the right tail. Earnings breadth is improving as AI capex trickles down to the Other 493 (earnings contribution up to 18%), and nominal GDP of 7% to 9% lets equities absorb higher rates.
tension_points.bear_case: 85% of S&P names are more than 10% below highs, the rally rests on ten stocks, correlation is at levels seen before the GFC and Volmageddon, and everyone is short the left tail at Sharpes near 14.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The OpenAI revenue shortfall reported by the FT challenging the AI demand premise, which the author says hits the narrow sleeve behind 70% of index gains.

tension_points.bull_case: Conciliatory Iran talk into the midterms would see energy and rate vol smoked off recent levels, favoring gold and IWM upside.
tension_points.bear_case: Refinery capacity is short regardless of oil flow through the Strait of Hormuz, the European emergency release covers only a little over a month, and a US diesel ban risk remains in a few months.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Peace talk would invalidate the energy premium and rate vol trade. A further energy price shock from resumed attacks or a US diesel ban would invalidate the benign rates view.
